correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the exact right-to-left group-labelled composition law (f,a)∘(h,b)=(f∘h,(b_i a_{h(i)})); idempotent labels on im(f) equal 1. The product P of commuting idempotents is an idempotent satisfying P E_j=P. Its label vector a defines diagonal D=(id,a), making D P D^-1=(p,1), after which the label comparison in (p,1)(D E_j D^-1)=(p,1) forces all conjugated labels to 1. The diagonal stabilizer of the base family comprises s_i=s_{p(i)}, precisely W^c, so orbit-stabilizer gives |W|^(n-c). The base projection is injective on any commuting-idempotent subsemigroup and its full lift set is one orbit. An independent nonabelian S3 enumeration identified 145 labelled idempotents over n=3, verified all 8,137 commuting ordered triples, direct gauge untwisting and rank profile {1:7884,2:252,3:1}. This finite check corroborates rather than proves the arbitrary W,k theorem.

value.rationale: Commuting idempotents encode compatible retractions and semilattices in finite transformation semigroups. The theorem identifies a genuinely uniform simultaneous normalization even for noncommutative group labels and supplies a natural exact fiber-count transfer across all finite arities, including semilattice maximality; this is a structural statement not just a single-idempotent renaming.

final_claim: For every finite (possibly nonabelian) group W and every finite commuting family of idempotents in W wr T_n, one diagonal unit simultaneously removes all labels. Above a specified base family with product rank c, the lift set is one W^n orbit of size |W|^(n-c) with stabilizer W^c; this extends to finite commuting-idempotent subsemilattices, their maximality and homogeneous G-sets.
